title: Hitcard buys control of Almaden in suspected backdoor listing
title_zh: 卡牌品牌Hitcard拟入主亚玛顿，疑似借壳上市

image.credit: Photo by Fearghal Kelly on Unsplash
image.author: Fearghal Kelly

lead: A trading-card maker backed by Pop Mart is buying a 20% stake in a struggling solar-glass company, a deal that looks less like an investment than a shortcut to the stock market.

paragraphs: Almaden (002623.SZ) said on the evening of November 2 that its controlling shareholder, Almaden Technology, plans to sell a 20% stake to Shanghai Qixing Network, which operates the adult collectible-card brand Hitcard. Should the deal close, the listed company's controlling shareholder and actual controller would both change. The two sides have signed a letter of intent, pricing remains undetermined, and trading was suspended from November 3. Notably, the stock had closed limit-up at 19.28 yuan the previous session.

The buyer's motives are plain enough. Hitcard has been reported to be preparing an IPO, but peers have fared badly: Kayou filed twice with the Hong Kong exchange, cleared its hearing in June 2025, then never launched a public offering, and its second application lapsed in October. Suplay's first filing expired in July. Against that backdrop, seizing control of an A-share company looks like a detour around the listing queue.

Almaden's controlling Lin family, by contrast, is under mounting strain. Solar glass generated 84.46% of revenue in 2025, and the sector's downturn has been brutal: revenue fell from 3.63 billion yuan in 2023 to 2.04 billion in 2025, with net losses of 127 million and 108 million yuan in 2024 and 2025. The first three quarters of 2026 brought a further loss of 145 million yuan.

Two attempts to absorb upstream supplier Fengyang Silicon Valley — valued at 2.525 billion yuan in 2021, then repriced at 1.25 billion in 2023 — were abandoned in 2022 and 2024 respectively. A $240 million plan to build a 500,000-tonne solar glass line in the UAE still awaits construction. Almaden Technology has already collected roughly 94.33 million yuan in pre-tax dividends, though 40 million of its shares remain pledged.

The announcement insists the change of control will not alter the core business, yet a diligence clause requires the buyer to verify whether the listed company can issue shares to acquire assets or undertake major restructuring — and to walk away with its 50 million yuan deposit if it cannot.
paragraphs_zh: 亚玛顿（002623.SZ）11月2日晚间公告，控股股东亚玛顿科技拟将20%股份转让给运营成人收藏卡品牌Hitcard的上海骑形网络。交易完成后，上市公司控股股东及实际控制人均将变更。双方已签署意向协议，价格尚未确定，股票自11月3日起停牌。值得注意的是，前一日该股已以19.28元涨停收盘。
买方的动机并不难猜。Hitcard此前传出筹备上市，但同行进展不顺：卡游两次向港交所递表，2025年6月通过聆讯后却未启动公开发售，第二次申请于10月失效；Suplay的首份申请也于7月届满。在此背景下，拿下A股公司控制权，更像是绕开上市排队的一条捷径。
相比之下，亚玛顿的林氏家族压力更大。2025年太阳能玻璃占其营收的84.46%，行业寒冬冲击剧烈：营收从2023年的36.28亿元降至2025年的20.36亿元，2024年、2025年分别亏损1.27亿元和1.08亿元，2026年前三季度再亏1.45亿元。
两次整合上游供应商凤阳硅谷的努力均告失败——2021年估值25.25亿元，2023年重启时作价降至12.50亿元，收购分别于2022年和2024年终止。公司另计划在阿联酋投资约2.4亿美元建设年产50万吨光伏玻璃产线，仍待落地。亚玛顿科技此前已获得约9433万元税前分红，但目前仍有4000万股处于质押状态。
公告强调控制权变更不会改变主营业务，但尽调条款却要求买方核查上市公司是否具备发行股份购买资产、重大资产重组等法定条件，若存在实质障碍，买方可终止协议并收回5000万元保证金。林氏家族保留14.90%股份，家族合计持股粗算约17.76%，差距仅2.24个百分点，借壳意图相当明显。
